outcome:
1. A structured data-backed analysis of membership assessment who are willing to apply to become managers. 
2. Create a proper structure for hiring new managers directly through recruitments, and automate to understand the perfect training mechanism for newer membership/managers and senior members who can be managers and/or current members who wish to be managers. 
3. Identifying the right manager's using the right personality types and utlizing the core aspects of that personality type while honing the weaker aspects.
details:
AIESEC Leadership Indexing of Personality Index (hence AIESEC LIPI) is basically the aspect of a manager or a leader that can be taken and measured for a person to understand how well do they fall under the different aspects of being a manager or a leader. As a framework this is to understand where they are lacking and what aspects of the point system where they are lacking and where they can be trained more in to become better managers.

Each personality profile has a set of Predictive Personality Index that, in general, can be corroborated to a manager or a leader. Hence each profile has a set of personalities that they can be strong or weak in. Using questions to assess each of these profiles, we will arrive with whether or not they are already good to be managers or what aspect of that needs to be trained much better before onboarding deeper into becoming the manager they intend to be. 
The review document of the person assessed will be automated and then shared as feedback to the VP and to the candidate as well. 
The sample doc. is here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/18zeBlsxg1epOKNi1yZ8yeigli8UKd8Qf/view

This is done in a period of 1 to 2 month (maybe more depending on the time period) to assess membership or during recruitments as well, to get a better idea of how they can be trained and honed. The training framework as well has certain general pointers and training methodologies that can be used, the next update on this would be collaborating the perfect training method with the lacking aspect.
kpis:
#. of members assessed
%age. implementation of JD and JS
notes:
Category: Membership Growth
Problem addressed: 1. Pipeline issues creating lack of pipeline towards important roles such as as EB
2. Issues related to manager training and assessment
3. Recruitment issues for hiring and recruiting managers directly without probation training alike to how organisation's hire manager interns with probation period for them.

outcome:
The GCP is majorly focussed towards:
1. better tracking mechanism for VP PM, LCP and 
2. Subsequently also as an accountability system between each VPs as well. 

This will also help in understanding and regular analysing of the MX Status of the LC, along with backlogs and good parts of each month.
details:
The steps that is to be followed:
1. The main sheet will be made a copy of for each month and for each month there will be a strict tracking of the MX Compliance that that department has done for the membership as well as for the MBs as well. 
2. The form first is rolled out to the MB where there will be important questions to understand percentage rating (out of 100%) about how much compliance and how much are they adhering to the MX Standards taught to them. 
3. Certain percentages from the form, and the filled out sheet together gives in the percentage that each department has followed or complied for MX in that particular month. 
4. The percentages of that will then be put in a report card for each department and will be sent to the VPs who can send it to their MBs as well. This will also be there in the monthly newsletter of PM. 

The standards, since are all closely interrelated, have been paired up in 3 distinct pairs:
a) Job Design and Job Support
b) Community and Community Engagement
c) Environment; Wellbeing and Team practices

Activities for each month are decided by the VP PM and the rest of the EB as well and they are stingently checked and tracked for each month. The activities are also given by the MB as well in the form that is rolled out. 

(for proof of how it works, a detailed video of the same is added in the link below: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rU7FbvBuYVO4j7wz-d7TrW797C9DJiHq/view?usp=sharing)
kpis:
KPI for the LC-PM Hub are:
1. % of MX Compliance each month
2. # of newsletters and report cards generated
3. % of succcessfully implemented activities 
4. Overall % of MX Tracking and Implementation in the LC
notes:
Category: Tools/Trackers/Frameworks
Problem addressed: As PM enters the MX tracking phase and understanding the different innovatios that PM can do for membership expereince, it is important for each LCs to understand and track the different methods of tracking the compliances and the coordination of various different activities for MX effeciently. Generally the problem occurs in reporting system for each departments and the LC as well. So the LC-PM Hub that I have created solves the problem of inconsistent tracking of MX Standards. This will also give a better understanding of the MX Tracking of each departments as well as a cumulative tracking of the LC as well. 

To put all of them into better points, the problems that this will solve:
1. Inconsistent Tracking
2. Cumulation of resources in a single pool
3. Understanding of PM Status and MX Status in individual departments and cumulative understanding for the entire LC
4. Generating Report Cards and Improvement Ratios for each department, MB and the LC as a while

outcome: We successfully piloted Leadership academy in 3 branches of Brigade Schools and raised 4.5 L as a result of the same. Apart from the revenue we facilitated growth in the 120 students enrolled with us. But the true outcome is the successful pilot of this program which has immaculate potential for the coming years as it just does not for this year but is recurring program every year. We have just tapped into 120 out of the 1800+ present in out target audience in the schools and every we have a chance to gain 4.5 - 6L just because of the program.
details:
Leadership Cell is an initiative by AIESEC in Bengaluru in association with Brigade School to inculcate leadership qualities, public speaking skills, social awareness and logical thinking in students in the 12 to 16 age group of students. 
Students are to go through a year filled with sessions, debates, MUNs, competitions, and growth maps to develop confidence and empathy for themselves and the people around them. 
This cell aims at inducing empathy in students to understand the hardships of life, parents, teachers, and strangers too. This is to develop a student's social skills during a susceptible period of adolescence so that the student grows into a considerate, compassionate, and logical adult.
kpis:
No. of students enrolled 
No. of students actively attending sessions
Feedback from students 
Constant growth in their LDA scores
Growth in their proactivity in class
notes:
Category: Portfolio Innovation
Problem addressed: We restructured Leadership Academy into Leadership Cell, Leadership Academy included both hard and soft skills and it was only a month program, when we initially tried to run the product the main backlash we faced were the following-
1. The duration of classes were insufficient
2. Hard skills could be taught anywhere and there were other platform who did with better HR and were more experienced.
3. No defined curriculum as such.
Looking at all these problems we restructured Leadership Academy into Leadership Cell, where we-
1. We made the program into a year long course about leadership and public speaking
2. We focused just on soft skills which were required for children to gain confidence and network effectively.
3. We made a curriculum, with set metrics to track every child's performance.

outcome: Gain in Registrations for Recruitments, Financial Growth, Improved Brand Image and better MXP funnel
details:
One of the biggest bottlenecks that we faced in recruitments in 2023.2 was the lack in registrations, the interest of people to join, decreased brand, reach, and unsatisfactory stakeholder experiences. The stakeholders who did not get selected after the interview process would spread negative comments about AIESEC and this would affect a brand image. Therefore, I came up with a plan or a project to improve value Delivery for the registration fee that the stakeholders pay. We conducted a five-day workshop on various topics such as marketing and sales, business model canvas, finance and finally a session about AIESEC where we talked about our experiences in AIESEC and how it has helped us grow. For each of the sessions conducted, there would be a certain task. For example, for the LinkedIn and networking session, the task given was to make a LinkedIn profile and we used the tasks as metrics to issue the certificate of excellence. Two certificates were issued, the certificate of participation and the certificate of excellence. This motivated the participants to work on their tasks and it also helped them build their skills in a way and empowered them. We had networking spaces after each session so the people could interact and have conversations that built a sense of community and AIESEC helped facilitate that.
The registration fee that was paid to join AIESEC as a member included the certification course. Therefore, even though some of the participants did not get selected, they left with the certificate certificate of participation. Hence, gaining something through AIESEC and finding value in the fee that they paid. We also pitched exchanges in one of the sessions which built us a foundation to kick-start branding and exchange performance, since we got a lot of leads there. 
This improved our brand image and brand reach immensely. The certification course also made it very easy for the Recruitment OC to pitch joining AIESEC which immensely improved the number of registrations that resulted in financial growth.
kpis:
1. The number of sessions conducted
2. The number of people attending the sessions
notes:
Category: Other
Problem addressed: The problem I am trying to solve is "decreasing registrations to join AIESEC" or I'm triyng to improve the number of registrations an entity can gain for financial sustainability, Membership Growth and IMPROVED BRAND IMAGE.

outcome: The major outcome of the GCP is identification and analysis of different risks every portfolio is exposed to and then reporting the same to the portfolio VPs to further take it up in their respective departments. The whole framework provided an effective method to tackle the crises of uncertainty and providing concrete action plan to all portfolios in order to reduce the particular risk they were exposed to.  It is also seen as a form of internal auditing by the FTF.
details:
The "Quarterly Risk Assessment Analysis " is a project taken up the FTF to identity and analyze risks every portfolio was is exposed to  and provide feedback/suggestions on a quarterly basis in order to keep the entity stable and provide protection against internal and external risks. The idea behind the whole project was taken from the IAB Reporting Framework that is done on a national level every six months. We tried to replicate the same framework at a local level but on a quarterly basis  to reap more benefits from the framework that worked well at the national level. The internal audit is done by the FTF who provide the reports to the portfolio VPs after collecting the monthly data, scrutinizing every information collected and then providing the suitable action plan for the same. The flow of analysis is as follows :

1. Monthly F o2o's for data collection 
2. Analysis within FTF with respect to data collected
3. Suggesting Way forward and Recommendations
kpis: #No of o20's taken, #No of FTF meetings done, #No of quarterly reports sent
notes:
Category: Tools/Trackers/Frameworks
Problem addressed: With the onset of Pandemic, the whole AIESEC entity in general was exposed to various kinds of risks. As the Finance Standards evolved by the second semester and introduced "Risk Management" as a standard, we took up this project specifically to identify, analyze and mitigate the possible risks  every portfolio in the LC was exposed to. In this way we were able to control and to some extend provide an action step/ measures to mitigate the risks.

The idea behind this CC was to bifurcate the major amount of work into 3 segments, each of which have their own set of specific job descriptions and a lot of room for the members to grow and learn in the additional work they choose to do.

The 3 segments for the CC are - iComm team, IR team & iVPP team
The iComm team being responsible for internal communications & engagement. 
The IR team being responsible for taking care of IR relations, generating promotional content & aiding in consideration.
The iVPP team is responsible for carrying out operational process for the iVPP pilot product by AIESEC International.

Each team allowed the members to focus on something more, and something different from the work they are already being allotted. 
Each of these teams are responsible for making sure that operations and engagement are both being taken care of, by the members, for the members.

The CC is primarily lead by Vansh Vashisht, LCVP iGTa for AIESEC in Chandigarh & Aakshi Aggarwal, Team Manager iGTa for AIESEC in Chandigarh. The 3 teams are further lead and guided by Team Leaders iGTa, Agrim Kalra & Pratham.

Category: Department Management

gcp_name: How to be a kick ass department Member?
outcome: The outcome of this GCP is a smooth and efficient transition for members. By providing the OGV Transition Booklet, we ensure that the process is streamlined and well-organized, covering all necessary details from customer interactions to pitching and attraction strategies. This comprehensive guide offers clarity, reducing stress and confusion for members and allowing them to focus on their new roles with confidence. It helps maintain continuity by preventing any loss of important information and enhances overall efficiency, saving time and effort. Ultimately, the booklet supports a successful transition of members.
details:
The booklet breaks down the EP`s journey in detail, starting with sign-ups, applying for opportunities, clearing interviews, and completing the exchange. Each step of the customer flow is explained, including crucial details about payments, visa assistance, and post-exchange debriefing. Additionally, the booklet places strong emphasis on attraction and sales strategies, highlighting the importance of targeted marketing campaigns, university relations, and consistent follow-ups to ensure leads are converted into approvals. The sales approach is rooted in building trust, effective storytelling, and addressing the specific needs of participants, whether it's gaining professional experience, building resumes, or traveling abroad.

The document also stresses the importance of team synergy, particularly with departments like marketing, to ensure smooth execution of the oGV process. Furthermore, it encourages members to adopt an entrepreneurial mindset, focusing on scaling the program by tapping into new markets and refining sales techniques.
kpis: The key performance indicator (KPI) for my GCP is proper transitioning of members and proper LEC
notes:
Category: Education
Problem addressed: This GCP aims to make the transition for outgoing global volunteers (OGVs) as smooth and resourceful as possible. The OGV Transition Booklet serves as a comprehensive guide, covering crucial elements such as customer interactions, value propositions, pitching techniques, and attraction strategies. By consolidating all this essential information into a single, well-organized resource, it ensures that every aspect of the transition is addressed efficiently. This approach helps prevent gaps and confusion, making the process more manageable and less stressful. Ultimately, it provides OGVs with a valuable tool that streamlines their transition and supports their success in their new roles.

details:
🔹Tracker Structure

1. Department
	•	Each of the 8 departments has its own section.
	•	Helps you filter or sort by department to see how teams are doing collectively.

2. TL (Team Leader)
	•	Every department is divided under TLs, with ~5 members each.
	•	TLs are directly accountable for updating and monitoring their members’ learning progress.

3. Modules
	•	Each column represents a learning module (e.g., Module 1: Introduction, Module 2: Skills, Module 3: Department-specific, Module 4: Advanced).
	•	You can mark completion as ✔, % done, or a date.
	•	This allows granular tracking of where each member stands.

4. Completion %
	•	Auto-calculated based on how many modules the member has finished.

🔹 Benefits
	•	Clarity: Everyone knows what stage each member is in.
	•	Accountability: TLs are clearly responsible for 5 members each.
	•	Scalability: Works well even as your LC grows beyond 85 members.
	•	Visual Progress: Helps EB/MB quickly spot problem areas.

🔹Dashboard
The Unified dashboard helps the PM and the LCP track how much of the minimum LEC has been downscaled by the TLs and measure the capacity of the members

details:
This GCP includes organizing a bootcamp for newly recruited GB (General Body) by the LCVP and the TL's. These quizzes act as checkpoints for understanding and retention while making the learning process more interactive.

Moreover, incorporating various team-building activities within the bootcamp is an excellent strategy. These activities foster camaraderie and teamwork among the GB members, emphasizing the importance of collaboration within the department. Strengthening these bonds early on can lead to a more cohesive and productive working environment as the members progress in their roles.

outcome: It helps MB members to stay focused, maximize productivity, and drive successful outcomes for the organizations while prioritizing their tasks
details:
A priority matrix, also known as a decision matrix or Eisenhower matrix, is a visual tool used to prioritize tasks or actions based on their importance and urgency. It helps individuals or teams make informed decisions about where to allocate their time and resources effectively.

A priority matrix typically consists of a grid divided into four quadrants, with importance represented on one axis and urgency on the other.
- urgent and important -do
- important and not urgent - schedule
- not important and urgent - delegate
-not urgent and not important - delete 

On the basis of this, the MB was asked to use this tool for prioritizing their tasks and increasing productivity by this tool , this was also provided to them , to use it further in their term .
kpis: Time management , workload distribution , segregation of tasks
notes:
Category: Tools/Trackers/Frameworks
Problem addressed: This tool was designed for the MB of AIESEC in Hyderabad , the purpose of this tool was to systematically organise the daily tasks according to priority , this was designed to solve to manage priorities and managing priorities is crucial for MB members to make effective use of time, align actions with goals, make informed decisions, mitigate risks, and coordinate team efforts.

outcome: Education about F&L standards and understand what goes on in different departments too
details:
A space taken at an LCM or LCong to introduce F&L Standards in a manner that it’s just not information being driven down and they remember it:
* Divide the LC into groups where there’s one person from each department (min) 
* Move to a hypothetical year and a hypothetical situation presenting the situation of the LC at that given point in time with respect to all aspects and departments. 
* Ask them to map out the risks present and come up with solutions (this ensures that they’re talking about departments which they’re not part of as well) 
* Present the risks you mapped out which they must’ve not as well and how you mitigate them 
* Give them another situation which is 2 months later than that done before with a different reality that the entity is facing at the time and repeat the same 
* Explain how an entity like yours faces innumerable risks on a daily basis and how the JD of F&L also takes care of Risk Management and why it’s so essential 
* Relate it to their personal lives as well as AIESEC departments 
* Tell them this is just 1/8th of what Finance & Legal entails as a portfolio and introduce the Standards. 

This way we introduce the set of F&L standards in a manner which ensures they would not forget them and actually realise the importance of the same whilst knowing more about other departments and having an active interest in F&L moving forward.

outcome: better structure to B2B, more data involved to perform tasks
details:
I believe that the role of a VP Marketing and B2B Manager should be evolved and molded into more of a marketing consultancy and brand strategist role where the core responsibilities include maintaining necessary brand image, focusing on CRM, and improvement of operational processes such as raising and consideration.

These standards provide a tangible system to track and upscale iCX operations. 
Brand perception: Having a detailed look at how AIESEC in Mumbai and its products are perceived, do we resonate with the feeling of limitlessness, and whether are we looked at as a leadership development organization. We try to answer these questions here.
Value Delivery: A study of how effectively we are providing the necessary deliverables which we promise based on the value proposition of AIESEC and its products. 
Marketing Metrics: Number of Email Campaigns run, output for Email Campaigns, Conversion rates, LinkedIn Campaigns, and the metrics for the same
Flow and Marketing Metrics: This is the same as above but also includes the customer flow metrics such as conversion ratios, number of opens, applicants, approvals, finished, and completes.
Client Satisfaction: We try to figure out if the clients/stakeholders are satisfied with our services. How many update/check-in calls are taken, response time from our as well as client’s end, are the clients happy with the kind of applicants, etc are the type of questions we try to answer here?
Engagement: Tracking number of attendees for IR events/expo, posters/engagement material sent per month, frequency of meets etc.
kpis:
All the standards above would have subquestions that can be answered by client/IR/VP iCX based on their understanding and reality. The answers would be in the form of a rating system out of 10. Each standard would end up having an average rating deduced out of 10 as well which later on would be summed up to have a total rating for B2B Standard (client/IR) presented out of 50. We can judge the health of B2B operations based on the net score that would be deduced. 
0-10: bad CRM and Image, lesser trust in AIESEC
10-20: CRM/Engagement is done but not adequately, not optimal for operations yet
20-30: CRM/Engagement is of good quality, frequency is an issue, the client is satisfied but services aren’t of the best nature yet
30-40: CRM/Engagement and frequency is on point, there may be issues with respect to the brand perception and stability
40-50: On point, good to go
Based on these scores the VPs can synergize and have a way forwards for individual portfolios to refine the way content marketing, email marketing, engagements, and brand value delivery is done.
Collection of data can happen through interviews, O2Os, meets, google forms, or any other means necessary keeping in mind that data collected should be accurate for meaningful deductions to be made.
notes:
Category: Tools/Trackers/Frameworks
Problem addressed: B2B not having a defined JD and it becoming too redundant

details:
According to me, taking 2 hour long STMs after a weeks gap has been proved redundant if we expect a dynamic working environment from the department and the MB members, everything, from setting up a meet, to sitting in the meeting for one to two exhausting hours seemed unproductive and indicated that the delay between setting every meet was making us lose a lot of time and on a lot of ideas as well. 

To help with this, I scrapped STMs and sent out a google invitation link for every two days scheduling am half an hour work call, where the team gets on a call, discusses problems, figures out CTAs and starts implementing it until the next work call. This was way better for improving performance and for team culture as well than the traditional method of giving out CTAs on whatsapp and wondering if the work was done or not. Not only this but this has been effectively downscaled to the MB members where they take such calls themselves and we finally have review meet for the dept at the end of the week to discuss the cumulative agenda.

details:
-After doing market research and analysis, a desk was set up at a place called “Jaggi” on the Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology Campus. 
-As Thapar is the primary market for AIESEC in Patiala, many factors were considered. 
-The location was chosen because it has many small eating joints where students from all years and faculty gather from 12 pm to 6 pm to hang out. The primary market for oGV was first year students who mostly came to this location during the above mentioned time. 
-The desk was set up every day for a week in coordination with the members and MB of the department. 
-A week before the desk was set up, and a form was circulated amongst the department members to make a schedule which allowed certain members from the department to be present for different slots between 12-6pm on the desk. 
-Small QR codes of GV were printed and circulated by the members to the people who came to Jaggi. 
-Members pitched the people coming on Jaggi and asked them to sign up or apply for a project. 
- A master pitch was created and shared with members as well. 
-After the desk, every night between 8-9pm, a working hour was conducted, which was organised for cold calling the leads generated and helping them apply for the projects they were interested in.

Category: Customer Flow
Problem addressed: The problems solved was lead generation and making leads apply for the projects.

outcome:
The outcome of the GCP pertained to exceeding the ideal HR capacity that was 52 and taking it to 59 with ease and raising INR 36,000 through recruitments.
The assurance of the qualitative nature of the leads was delivered through their interview analysis that was inclusive of Department+Reality based customised questions.
details:
The REC OC was announced merely 1 month prior and along with the launch, because the reality of the entirety of the LC wishing to leave was known, pocket recruitment cycle had begun on the side. In this pocket recruitment cycle, the LC was made to refer people that they deemed were good fits for AIESEC in South Mumbai. These people were directly interviewed for the Managerial Positions. While these people remained as GB members till the MB applications rolled out, they were selected after their application was approved and deemed worthy. 
Simultaneously, the REC OC had begun creating posters that were completely reality dependent - Christmas+New Year+Marvel based posters and during the pitches to leads, it was ensured that emphasis was given on forming potential and strong bonds, learning to enjoy the art of professionalism and being provided with the capacity to lead teams in the near future. This allowed us to offer more than just a leadership-oriented approach to our leads which was not observed earlier. This enabled us to get 140+ people to apply out of which 93 were interviewed. 36 people were accepted as potential AIESECers and 34 of them paid the membership fees and got selected. The numbers advocate the qualitative aspect of the recruitments and this was only possible due to lead nurturing orientations that were held each week along with feedbacks for the same being rolled out so that the leads felt heard.
We ensured that through these orientations, they realised the true worth of AIESEC along with knowing how they would benefit from it with real life examples and experiences. This was the only factor that made 34 out of 36 selected people pay.
kpis:
1) Utilising College MOU to acquire leads.
2) Tapping into colleges such as Jai Hind and HR for the first time and acquiring a huge amount of leads
3) Tapping into engineering  colleges such as VESIT so as to include the domain of engineering in AIESEC and introduce AIESEC to engineering students that applied in good quantities in the later half of the rec cycle.
notes:
Category: Membership Growth
Problem addressed: 1) Reviving the entire and complete strength of the LC as only 2 members were retained.
2) Balancing and focusing on qualitative as well as the quantitative aspects of recruitments
3) Rebuilding the previously tainted brand image of AIESEC in South Mumbai in the market
4) Coming up with deliverables that were somewhat inclusive of appealing personally -youth oriented-incentives and ceasing to centre marketing campaigns only and only around leadership development to counter the problem of losing leads over the course of time.

outcome: Members received feedback on how to pitch better as bottlenecks in member's pitches were solved. The considerations and attractions team understood the full scope of the CX & IR team's contribution to the department.
details:
XPDF was conducted on 2 days, the first day was to train the CX & IR team in conducting preparation, experience and post experience standards, along with collecting and submitting legalities (cover letter and insurance letter). The CA (considerations and attractions) team acted as EP's and were given specific personas in advance, which were based partly on past EP's experiences. For example, one of the members was assigned the persona of a nervous and anxious girl, who has many doubts during OPS. During the exchange program she enjoys her time there but is dissatisfied with her work, she does not communicate her availability well, she also feels unsafe because of the presence of a guy who is being creepy. Her persona for debrief was that she overall enjoyed the exchange as all the problems she was facing earlier were solved. Each CA member was given a persona and was put into a breakout room with their respective EPM, who conducted the OPS, PGS, EP update, and DwA/RIS with them. The team scored them on factors defined for each space
For day two, the EB was called to be leads for the CA team, who had to pitch the product, find a suitable project and get their lead approved within a span of 35 minutes. They had to refer to the resource hub for national and local searchtools to pitch available projects. Google form was created to apply to the project and pay the money.
kpis:
CX & IR: a 5 point grading system for each space (OPS, PGS, EP updates, DwA/RIS)
CA: a 5 point grading system for the pitch
notes:
Category: Education GCP
Problem addressed: Knowledge downscaling, pitching, preparation, experience and post-experience standards delivery

outcome:

VP's understanding about Financial state and the various consequences of the same

details:
The performance analysis report is a financial awareness report for the Front Office and BD VP’s to exactly understand their financial performance in the present month.
It allows them to understand their performance in terms of their T vs A that they have submitted to the national end through various graphs and charts

Front Office- It gives them a representation of the entity targets with regards to Sign Ups, Approved, Realized and Completes which allows them to understand their standings at the national level.
BD- It gives the portfolio a representation of their targets in terms of revenue raised and youth recognized and their standings at the national level.

Second part of the report is all about the Financial Data for the LC in the present month which allows the VP’s to understand the Current & Reserve Bank Balance, Debt Ratio, Net Profit Ratio and the standing internal liability of the LC.
It shows them the income and expenditure B vs A which helps them understand how their portfolio performed financially throughout the month.

After reporting the financial data, it allows them to understand the financial state of the LC by making them understand the new recon model and the concept of performance recon and CPE essentially. This allows them to understand why they should be consistently performing, by showing a clearance pattern of recon as well.

Usage of words in RED allows them to understand the importance of the financial state as well and mentioning the consequences of the same like Entity in Debt.

Last but not the least it gives the VP’s their respective targets after much calculations and financial analysis for the upcoming month.
The report ends with a CTA for the VP’s where they have to fill in a calendar database on notion with their respective Plan of Action for the coming week, and mentioning their targets for the week. This helps the LCP and LCVP F&L hold them accountable for these targets and constantly track their performance as the calendar being a live one allows continuous observation.
At the end of the week, LCP along with the LCVP F&L have a review call with the respective VP’s to take a sensing of the rate of completion of their targets and help them understand the way forwards for the same.
kpis:
Financial Awareness among the VP's
Efficient Tracking Mechanisms
B vs A
Operational & BD Income
notes:
Category: Tools/Trackers/Frameworks
Problem addressed: Low B vs A
Low Operational & BD Income

details:
It is an opportunity for the students to engage in the activity of a life-sized version of a classical board game, Monopoly with a surprise treasure hunt.

Steps -


- All attendees will be divided into clans. 
- A monopoly bank will be allocated an equal amount of game money to start them off with.
- For every venue purchase and rent fee they will be in charge of the monetary transactions 
  which will enable them with financial decision making skills and be  more sustainable as a 
  team. 
- Each team will progress according to the number they get with each dice roll. 
- Every Time they cross the start point after the game has begun, the clans will get a certain 
  amount of money.
- As one round reaches a halfway point, a treasure hunt will begin. Clus related to SDGs will 
  guide them to the final treasure.
- They will hence be given an option to choose between a mystery box or money and the 
  mystery box will contain cards like get of jail, skip a chance, etc.

outcome: Increased product knowledge of the membership
details:
Project Reelisations is a stimulation environment, created for the members to perform the tasks that take place in each phase of customer flow and each stage in the process flow.
In the consideration phase, 
- They're required to make a pitch call, pipeline meet followed by getting the NOC signed.
- They then contact the IR responsible, send the EP resume and schedule an interview. 
In the preparation phase, 
- They submit the required documents and obtain the insurance. 
- Book the flight tickets, Deliver an OPS and register of VISA and share the AEPP.
In the experience phase, 
- The EP manager is given certain situations and problems for which they'll be presenting the solutions.
- The situations are the common problems that the EP might face, which might lead to RE break (Ex: JD mismatch, incorrect work-duration, etc.)
kpis: On time execution of all SOPs in each stage of the Customer Flow
notes:
Category: Customer Flow
Problem addressed: Due to the virtual context, a lot of the new members, have zero idea about the processes of the Customer Flow. In order to provide a sound platform for the membership to understand and practically experience the stages in the Customer Flow, we've designed a safe environment for members by replicating everything that happens in an actual realization.
